title: Finite Q3 onsite weighted isometry and endpoint-to-edge bond recurrence reduction
question: Does the exact finite Q3 onsite flow preserve the two-orientation local energy-weighted seminorm, leaving only a finite endpoint-to-edge bond multiplier for the graph recurrence?
method: Build the registered quartic Q3 onsite and bond matrices on the two-site local algebra associated with the volume-2 edge, volume-4 square, and volume-6 2x3 graph fixtures.
Shift the onsite and onsite-plus-bond Hamiltonians spectrally to positive weights and evaluate both K^(1/2) A K^(-1/2) and K^(-1/2) A K^(1/2) orientations for four deterministic local probes.
Conjugate each probe by the exact finite spectral onsite unitary and check the commuting-weight isometry, then conjugate by both signs of the full quartic bond unitary.
Use the two orientation weighted conjugation factors as the finite product-envelope multiplier and compare the primary and non-importing independent lanes row by row.
Compile Lean R299 for the commuting-weight identity, the two-orientation multiplier association, and the declared rational recurrence fixture.
finding: Primary 396/396, independent 395/395, integrated 26/26, and Lean R299 PASS. The finite onsite commutator and unitarity residuals are at numerical zero for every declared volume. The maximum and minimum bond multiplier on every volume row are 1.10647614122132 for both bond orientations in this local fixture. Thus the finite exact-Q3 layer reduces the tested recurrence to an endpoint-to-edge inclusion factor together with the bond multiplier; no volume- or cutoff-uniform inclusion bound is supplied.
decision_reason: The onsite part of the finite split is not the source of growth when its weight is generated by the same onsite Hamiltonian: spectral commutation gives an exact two-orientation isometry. The remaining finite bond rows are consistent with the abstract product envelope, but the endpoint-to-edge weight transfer and its source, volume, cutoff, beta, and common-core uniformity are still independent proof obligations.
